21 A wave travels on the surface of water. P, Q, R and S are four particles of water on the surface.
The diagram shows the positions of the particles at one instant. The direction of travel of the
wave is from left to right.
direction of wave travel
P
R
Q
S
Which two particles are about to move upwards?
A
P and R
B
P and S
C
R and S
D
Q and S

hints: Notice the wave profile moves from left to right but particles P, Q, R and S only vibrate vertically, so compare the height just to the left of each particle with its present height.
Imagine the whole sine-like shape shifted a small distance to the right and ask whether the new curve at each particle dot is higher or lower.
Check Q on the downward slope through equilibrium, R on the upward slope through equilibrium, P at the crest and S at the trough for up versus down change.
walkthrough: This is a transverse water wave, so each surface particle moves up and down while the wave pattern travels from left to right.
To find the next motion, shift the whole wave a little to the right. The displacement that was just to the left of a particle will arrive at that particle.
At Q, the curve to the left is higher because Q is just to the right of crest P on a falling slope, so the arriving displacement is higher and Q moves up.

At R, the curve to the left is lower because R is coming up from a trough on a rising slope, so the arriving displacement is lower and R moves down. At P the crest moves right so P moves down, and at S the trough moves right so S moves up.
Therefore the two particles whose displacement increases are Q and S. This is option D.

A.explanation: P is at a crest and R is on the rising slope through equilibrium, and both will move downwards as the rightward wave advances.

B.explanation: S will move upwards from the trough, but P at the crest is about to move downwards.

C.explanation: S will move upwards, but R on the rising slope is about to move downwards toward the approaching trough.

D.explanation: Q on the falling slope and S at the trough both gain a higher displacement when the profile shifts to the right, so both move upwards.
